legend: ✅ built in, or in an official package of the same project (named) · ⚠️ partial, opt-in, with a caveat, or through a third-party package (named) · ❌ not built in · 🔜 planned by the maintainers, no code yet · — does not apply. Every cell was checked against the source of the published package in October 2026.

decodeChecks.note: Any well-formed value comes back; checking its shape is left to the program.

noEval.note: `index.js:470` compiles every serializer (EvalError in a realm without code generation). A `mode: 'standalone'` module runs there, but `anyOf`/`oneOf`/`if` also need `inlineValidators: true` or Ajv compiles at runtime.

schemaData.note: The README's security notice: schemas are compiled into code, so a schema from a peer is not safe to build.

validation.note: Only `required` and array shapes throw. `pattern`, `minimum`, `enum` and `format` are ignored, `'false'` in a boolean → `true`, and a `const` field writes the constant whatever the value.

decodeChecks.note: Bad indices and unknown tags throw `Error('Invalid input')`/`Unknown type`, but `["BigInt","abc"]`, `["RegExp","("]`, `["URL","x"]` throw raw SyntaxError/TypeError, `Temporal.*` tags throw ReferenceError on Node 24, and `["Date",5]` is accepted as a Date.

depth.note: `hydrate` (src/parse.js:71) recurses: a 14 KB flat payload of ~2,200 nested arrays (Node 24 default stack) throws a raw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`; `stringify` and `uneval` overflow too on deep values.

version.note: capnp-es is the maintained fork (unjs) of capnp-ts; its README calls it alpha quality. capnp-ts itself was revived in 2026 (0.9.3).

schemaData.text: schema nodes as capnp messages; no dynamic codec

envelope.text: segment framing carries no type id

unknownFields.text: kept in the buffer; `copyFrom` copies them

decodeChecks.text: pointer and bounds checks; some raw RangeErrors
decodeChecks.note: Library errors (`CAPNP-TS019`, `TS024`) for bad pointers, but an empty buffer and a huge Text length throw raw `RangeError`s, and the frame header is trusted before its size check (see limits).

errorPath.text: message with a pointer address, no field path

depth.text: lazy reads; deep copy → raw RangeError
depth.note: Reads do not recurse and the traversal limit stops a pointer cycle (`CAPNP-TS022`), but the nesting limit defaults to `MAX_INT32`: `setRoot`/`copyFrom` of a 100 000-deep message overflows the stack.

limits.note: It counts pointer objects per Message, so one legit Message re-read ~4.2 M times throws. The segment count in the frame header is allocated (`Array.from`, `BlZmb8ia.mjs:818`) before it is checked: 8 bytes claiming 2^32-1 segments start a multi-billion-element allocation.

validation.note: Tested on the generated-code shape: a missing struct field writes 0, a number in a string field writes `""`, `null` throws a raw TypeError. The dynamic `RecordWriter` checks shapes, enums and missing fields, not scalar types.

zeroCopy.text: decodes the whole record (bytes are views)

otherLanguages.text: C#, Rust, C++, C, Dart, Python

unknownFields.text: ignored: skips to the message end

decodeChecks.text: no bounds checks: garbage or raw RangeError
decodeChecks.note: Tested: a truncated buffer throws DataView `RangeError`; a string length past the end decodes to `"A\u0000"`.

limits.note: A `bool[]` length prefix is trusted: 13 bytes decoded into a 100 000 000-element array in 1.2 s (up to 2^32 possible).

schemaData.text: plain JSON, but keys become code

validation.text: typeof and range checks, on by default
validation.note: `build(schema, false)` drops them: a string in a `uint8` field then encodes as 0. With checks on, 3.7 in an int field becomes 3, NaN passes float checks, a missing string throws Node's ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE.

depth.text: no recursive types; depth fixed by schema

limits.note: A 4-byte payload for a `buffer` field yields a 268 MB Buffer.

noEval.note: From the 4th read of a record structure the reader is compiled with `new Function` (`unpack.js:501`), also by the default `unpack` on a payload that defines records in-message. A throw is caught and code generation is switched off for the process (still a CSP violation report). `msgpackr/index-no-eval` (a UMD build, `dist/index-no-eval.cjs`) never calls it.

otherLanguages.text: any MessagePack library; records are msgpackr-only

envelope.text: record ids only; structures kept out of band

decodeChecks.note: Truncation gives "Unexpected end of MessagePack data". In 3 000 random byte mutations 1–5% escaped as raw TypeError/RangeError/SyntaxError (e.g. `read(...).map is not a function`, a pointer ext without a reference map); the reserved byte 0xC1 decodes to a `C1` sentinel object instead of an error.

depth.note: Recursive `read()` with no depth limit. `checkedRead` marks any RangeError `incomplete` (`unpack.js:225`), so `UnpackrStream` treats a deep message as a partial one: it emits nothing, buffers, and stalls until `maxIncompleteBufferSize` (64 MB) is exceeded. `pack` of a deep value also overflows.

limits.note: Array/map lengths are checked against the remaining bytes (no allocation from a small header), but there is no option for string, array, map or depth limits.

otherLanguages.text: MessagePack in C, Go, Python, Rust, Java…

recursive.text: any nesting on decode; no cycles

flags.text: typed arrays as raw `bin`, type lost

noEval.text: probes `new Function` at import; compiles records
noEval.note: `decode.js:47` runs `new Function('')` when the module loads (a CSP report even if records are never used) and compiles record readers from the 4th read (`decode.js:532`). If the probe throws, records use the slow path. `cbor-x/index-no-eval` never calls it.

otherLanguages.text: any CBOR library; records are cbor-x-only

decimals.text: tag 4 decoded to a float; not encoded

rename.text: names travel (`keyMap` maps names to numbers)

envelope.text: record ids only; structures kept out of band

decodeChecks.note: Truncation gives "Unexpected end of CBOR data". In 3 000 random byte mutations 5–7% escaped as raw TypeError/RangeError (e.g. "Cannot create property 'slowReads' on string", "byte length of Float32Array should be a multiple of 4"); a record key that is a BigInt reaches `JSON.stringify` and throws a TypeError.

depth.note: Recursive `read()` with no depth limit. `checkedRead` marks any RangeError `incomplete` (`decode.js:239`), so `DecoderStream` treats a deep message as a partial one: it emits nothing and keeps buffering, with no size cap. `encode` of a deep value also overflows.

limits.note: Process-wide, not per decoder; defaults 112 810 000 / 16 810 000. `maxObjectSize`, documented in the README, is never read by the decoder, record objects bypass `maxMapSize`, and there is no string or depth limit.

errorPath.text: message only; some name the field

limits.text: none (size header must match the buffer)

otherLanguages.text: V8 only

recursive.text: any nesting; cycles and shared refs

decodeChecks.note: Truncated, garbage and huge-length inputs all throw `Unable to deserialize cloned data.`; there is no shape to check.

depth.note: Measured on a hand-built nested array with the default stack; `v8.serialize` itself throws `RangeError` past ~3 280 levels.

keysOnWire.text: text: each time; binary: once (symbol table)

otherLanguages.text: Java, C, Python, Rust, Go, .NET

unions.text: any value; annotations can tag it

decodeChecks.note: IonSpan.js:165-170 returns EOF (-1) past the end instead of throwing: a 55-byte value cut to 13-27 bytes loads as `null`, cut to 52 bytes loads with a different timestamp. The text parser rejects truncated input.

depth.note: `load` of 100 000 nested lists or s-expressions, and `dumpText`/`dumpBinary` of a deep or cyclic value, throw `Maximum call stack size exceeded`. The raw `Reader` cursor steps in 100 000 levels fine.

proto.note: Fields live in `Object.create(null)` (dom/Struct.js:10), so `get('__proto__')` works and nothing global is touched. `toJSON()` copies them onto `Object.create(Struct.prototype)` with `obj[key] =`: `__proto__` replaces the prototype and the fields after it vanish (`JSON.stringify` gives `{}`).

streaming.text: `Reader` steps through values; whole input in memory
